title: aidd item types
description: The format of schemas/item-types.json: one row for each type of thing aidd tracks or writes, with its group, its form, its id, its folder, its templates, its schema, and its statuses. A new type is a row and no code that lists types. A schema or a skill that must spell a list of types out has a test that holds it equal to the rows.

groups.description: The groups `aidd new --list` prints, each a key and the words `aidd new --list` says it by, in the order it prints them. A group says how `aidd new` writes its types.

common_documents.description: The documents `aidd new --help` names after the work items, one or more for each role that writes most, in the order it names them. Each is a type of `types`.

types.description: One row for each type, keyed by the word a person types in `aidd new <type>` and the value of a front matter's or a Spec `docs` entry's `type`. The order of the rows is the order `aidd new` lists the types in.

template.description: A file name in the skill's `assets/`, with no folder.

group.description: The key of the group `aidd new --list` files the type under. It decides how `aidd new` writes it.

form.description: `work_item`: a Spec, an Intent, or a proposal, which has a status group and a next step. `typed_document`: another file whose front matter's top-level `type` names it. `document`: a file with no `type` of its own.

noun.description: The type as a sentence names it, with its article, such as `a Spec`.

backlog.description: True for a work item that a delivery team owns and that other work waits for, with `blocked_by` and a parent: a Spec and an Intent.

id_prefix.description: The prefix of the id `aidd new` numbers, such as `SPEC` for `SPEC-<n>`. A type with none takes the id a person gives.

parent.description: The one type this type's `parent` names. Each is a type of `types`.

schema.description: The schema of the type's front matter, a file in `schemas/`.

statuses.description: Where the type's status words are: a schema file and a pointer to the node that holds `enum`, `x-meanings`, and `x-groups`.

explained_by_schema.description: True when `aidd explain <type>` answers with the first sentence of the type's schema. Another type is answered from `loop.documents` in `schemas/roles.json`, or not at all.

inside_work_item.description: True for a document that lives in a work item's folder and is never a work item itself, whatever its front matter says.

folder.description: Where the type's files live. `{specs}`, `{proposals}`, and `{docs}` stand for the config's `specs_dir`, `proposals_dir`, and `docs.dir`, and the config key wins over its default. `<loop.documents>` says `loop.documents.<type>.files` in `schemas/roles.json` gives the one folder. A path with none of them is the same in every repository. A type with no folder has its files in `files`, or lives beside its Spec, or has the place the command that writes it gives.

templates.description: The templates `aidd new` starts the type from, by variant. `default` is the one every type has; `short`, `living`, and `change_order` are the variant a command picks for a short Spec, a living plan, and a contract's change order.

files.description: The files of a document the repository has one of, each at a path with `{docs}` for the docs folder, or `<loop.documents>` for the one path `schemas/roles.json` gives, and the template it starts from. A file with no `.md` template is copied as it is.

next.description: What `aidd new` says to do next once it has written the type.

without_spec.description: Why a document that no one Spec links refuses `--spec`.
